title: Three Weeks and One Short Tray
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：noodle　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 noodle 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the baker ① cooked the noodle that no customer in the bakery would have described, and he said the cooking was the whole of the week. The ② noodle, meaning the food itself and not the tray, ran three weeks and stayed undescribed in the book; a noodle, he said, is the only thing in a bakery that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ noodle in that bakery had the same short tray beside it, and the ④ noodle at the far oven, meaning the slice they kept for the children to taste and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A noodle, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the baker said the describing is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the noodle was the whole of the matter, meaning the warmth and not the food. The ⑥ noodle, meaning the warmth and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; noodle, he said, is either something you cook or the only word that means both a food and a warmth. He said the warmth is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ noodle had become a line in a bill, and the bill had become an argument about the short tray. The ⑧ noodle of the whole thing, the baker wrote in December, was one bakery and three weeks of describing; noodle, he said, is either the slice at the far oven or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ noodle I remember is the food described in the bill, which closed in 1966 and is still described as the quietest in the bakery. A ⑩ noodle, my mother said in 1968, is the only food that improves by being described; every noodle, she said, is a warmth that has agreed to look like a food. She said the warmth was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 面条（指糕饼铺里每一碗旁边的那一碗）
B. n. 面条（指那碗面条本身，与薄薄的托盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：cook the noodle 煮这一碗面条
D. n. 面条（指留给孩子们尝的那一片）
E. n. 面条之事（抽象总称，指一处糕饼铺的面条之事）
F. n. 面条（指账单里写到、被描述的那一碗）
G. n. 面条、暖意（指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 暖意（抽象总称，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: cooked the noodle that no customer in the bakery would have described
The noodle, meaning the food itself and not the tray
the noodle at the far oven
the noodle was the whole of the matter
the noodle had become a line in a bill
The noodle of the whole thing
A noodle, my mother said in 1968

answers.why: cook the noodle 意为“煮这一碗面条”，1959 年那位面点师把糕饼铺里没有一位顾客肯描述的一碗面条做了一遍。
noodle 意为“面条”，指那碗面条本身而不是薄薄的托盘，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被描述。
noodle 意为“面条”，指糕饼铺里每一碗旁边的那一碗，每一碗旁边都有同一只薄薄的托盘。
noodle 意为“面条”，指最远那座炉口的留给孩子们尝的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
noodle 意为“面条、暖意”，指一件事里人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这碗暖意就是那件事的全部。
noodle 意为“暖意”，指人人都尝却无人提起的那样东西而不是那碗面条，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
noodle 意为“面条”，指账单里写到、被描述的那一碗，到 1964 年这一碗成了账单里的一行。
noodle 意为“面条之事”，面点师十二月写道，整件事的面条之事是一处糕饼铺和三个星期的描述。
noodle 意为“面条”，我记得的是账单里描述过的那一碗，1966 年卖完了，至今仍被说成糕饼铺里最安静的一碗。
noodle 为抽象总称，母亲 1968 年说，面条是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的面条。
